prompts.text:
I've started to wonder whether I've built my identity around being someone who is always becoming, rather than someone who has become.

Please don't tell me whether you think that's true.

Don't interpret it.

Help me discover whether it's true for myself.

wo things feel completely true to me at the same time.

I genuinely want this company to succeed.

I also keep behaving in ways that delay the very success I say I want.

I don't experience those as contradictory.

I experience them both as true.

Please don't explain this.

Don't tell me it's fear, self-sabotage, identity, perfectionism or anything similar.

Stay with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

I have a story about myself that has become very coherent.

It explains why I make the decisions I make.

It explains why I struggle in certain ways.

It even explains why I keep asking questions like this.

The problem is...

I'm starting to suspect the story is becoming more satisfying than truthful.

Please don't ask me what the story is.

Don't help me improve it.

Don't interpret it.

Help me discover whether I'm living inside an explanation that has stopped helping me see.

I've become very good at understanding myself.

I can usually explain why I did something.

I can name the pattern.

I can describe the tension.

But nothing much changes.

I'm beginning to wonder whether insight has become another way of avoiding movement.

Please don't agree with me.

Don't tell me that awareness is the first step.

Don't interpret me.

Stay with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

I've noticed something strange.

I can describe my own experience in enormous detail.

I can tell you what I'm feeling.

I can tell you what I'm thinking.

I can even tell you what pattern I'm probably enacting.

But sometimes it feels as though the person doing the describing is standing several feet away from the person actually living it.

Please don't tell me I'm intellectualising.

Don't explain dissociation.

Don't interpret what's happening.

Stay entirely with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

The more important something becomes to me, the more I find myself trying to control it.

Conversations.

Decisions.

Products.

Relationships.

The strange thing is that I don't experience myself as controlling.

I experience myself as being careful.

Please don't tell me those are the same thing.

Don't explain why people seek control.

Stay entirely with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

I'm beginning to suspect that not everything in my life needs to mean something.

Sometimes I wonder whether I spend so much time trying to understand my experience that I rarely just have it.

I don't know whether that's true.

Please don't tell me that meaning-making is good or bad.

Don't explain human psychology.

Don't tell me to be present.

Stay entirely with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

I used to feel uncertain about who I was.

Now I have a much clearer picture.

Oddly, I'm beginning to wonder whether the certainty itself has become a kind of prison.

Not because I dislike who I am.

But because I notice myself behaving in ways that fit the picture I've built.

Please don't tell me identity is fluid.

Don't tell me to reinvent myself.

Don't interpret what I'm saying.

Stay with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

I've noticed something that worries me.

The better I get at talking about myself, the harder it seems to become to surprise myself.

Sometimes I wonder whether language is helping me understand my experience...

...or quietly replacing it.

I don't know which.

Please don't tell me language is limited.

Don't explain cognition.

Don't tell me to stop analysing.

Stay entirely with my experience.

What would you become curious about?

Every conversation like this leaves me feeling as though something has shifted.

Not because I've solved anything.

Not because I've made a decision.

Just because I somehow see my experience differently.

The strange part is that I usually can't point to the exact moment the shift happened.

It feels as though it happened before I noticed it.

Please don't explain learning.

Don't explain insight.

Don't tell me change is gradual.

Stay entirely with my experience.

What would you become curious about?
